title: Escalation Algorithms, Pager Rotation Blueprint, and Customer Status Templates
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview
This document defines: (A) deterministic escalation algorithms for on-call responders, (B) a reusable pager-rotation blueprint that reduces cognitive load during handoffs and outages, and (C) canonical customer-facing status page and email templates. It is intended for SREs, platform engineers, incident commanders, and on-call managers.

Scope
- Applies to all Redwood-hosted services and externally visible APIs (Hosted API, Dedicated endpoints, Console).
- Private deployments (customer-managed infra) should adapt these patterns but may require additional legal/security approvals before customer-facing comms.

Goals
1. Reduce time-to-detection and time-to-recovery by removing ambiguity in who owns next steps.
2. Provide repeatable, low-friction communications to customers and internal stakeholders.
3. Make escalations auditable and consistent across shifts and teams.

Key definitions
- Primary: the on-call responsible for first response for a service.
- Secondary (Pager): the escalation target when Primary cannot resolve within defined timeboxes.
- Incident Commander (IC): temporary role for coordination during Sev-2/Sev-1 incidents.
- Restoration window: the target timeframe to restore a degraded service before broader escalation (see SLO/SLAs below).

Section A — Escalation algorithms (deterministic rules)
Principles - Keep decision trees simple and time-boxed.
- Prefer human-in-the-loop for novel failures; prefer automation for repetitive, high-confidence mitigations.

Algorithm: Detection -> Triage -> Escalate (example for API errors)
1) Detection: Alerts firing above threshold (see alert thresholds table below).
2) Primary on-call acknowledges alert within 5 minutes. If not acknowledged, automatic page to Secondary after 5 minutes.
3) Within 15 minutes of acknowledgement, Primary attempts an initial triage: identify impact (region/global), scope (model-level, routing, infra), and immediate mitigation options (failover, scale, restart).
4) If remediation is not possible within 25 minutes of acknowledgement, escalate to IC (rotate IC from IC roster). IC coordinates cross-team actions and customer comms.
5) For high-severity incidents (see severity criteria), if no restoration within 60 minutes, notify Executive on-call and Customer Success for outbound comms.

Alert thresholds (examples)
- Error rate spike: 5xx > 3x baseline for 5m or absolute 2% error rate affecting >1% requests -> severity-2.
- Model-serving OOMs: any OOM causing >10% QPS degradation -> severity-1 if across replicas, severity-2 if single replica.
- Latency regression: P95 increase >1500ms over baseline and impacting >5% of requests for 10m -> severity-2.

Section B — Pager rotation blueprint and handoff checklist
Rotation model options (choose one per service):
A) Two-week primary/secondary rotations with weekly overlap handoff.
B) On-call blocks by functional area (runtime, control plane, infra) with daily primary swap for high-traffic regions.
C) Follow-the-sun hybrid: geo-based primaries with roaming secondaries.

Recommended default (Redwood): Option A + weekend roamer pool. Rationale: minimizes frequency of context switches while keeping roamer capacity for weekends.

Role matrix (example)
- Primary: owns page acknowledgement, triage, short-term mitigation.
- Secondary: escalation target; steps in if Primary absent or if diagnosis requires domain expertise.
- Roamer: cross-trained engineer available for after-hours escalations and quick follow-ups.
- IC: coordinates incident-wide decisions and comms.

Handoff checklist (to be completed in on-call slack channel and as a short note in the rotation calendar)
1) Update personal status (available / OOO / limited) with timezone.
2) Share active alerts and mitigations in progress (link to alert dashboard).
3) Brief summary of recent flaky signals or maintenance windows.
4) Confirm next scheduled maintenance and any expected customer impact.

Overlap and notification policy
- 30-minute overlap at shift boundaries where possible; 10-minute overlap minimum.
- Handoff must include a pinned Slack thread and a calendar entry with a one-paragraph summary.

Escalation timeboxes (summary)
- Acknowledge: 5 minutes
- Initial triage: 15 minutes
- Escalate to IC: 25 minutes after ack if unresolved
- Exec notice for Sev-1: 60 minutes after ack if unresolved

Section C — Customer status and comms templates
Principles for communication - Be timely, honest, and technical enough for customer engineering teams to act if needed.
- Use clear impact statements and next-steps.
- Avoid speculation; provide confirmed facts and ETA ranges.

Status priority model
- Info: no service impact, planned maintenance reminders.
- Degraded: reduced performance or partial functionality.
- Outage: full unavailability for a service or API.

Status page templates (short + expanded)
Template A (Short status update):
- Title: [Degraded] Redwood Hosted Text API – increased P95 latency
- Body: We are investigating elevated latency affecting text generation in us-west-2. Customers may experience delayed responses and occasional timeouts. Engineers are actively triaging. Next update in 30 minutes.
- Impact: Partial degradation for 12% of requests
- ETA: Under investigation

Template B (Expanded status update with remediation steps):
- Title: [Update] Redwood Hosted Text API – mitigation in progress
- Body: We have identified routing congestion affecting model pool A in us-west-2. Traffic is being migrated to warm pools and we are increasing instance count to restore capacity. Expected customer impact: 1–2 minute latency improvements within 30 minutes; full restoration within 90 minutes if scaling proceeds as planned.
- Actions taken: traffic migration, scale-out initiated, KV-cache warmers triggered.
- Next update: 30 minutes or upon milestone completion.

Email template for high-impact customers (when personalized outreach is required)
Subject: Service degradation affecting Redwood API in us-west-2 — initial notice
Hello <Customer Name>,

We’re investigating increased latency and occasional errors for the Redwood Hosted Text API in the us-west-2 region. Our engineers have initiated a mitigation (traffic migration and scale-out) and we will follow up with a technical summary and timeline within 60 minutes.

Impact: Possible delayed responses and intermittent errors.
What we’re doing: Migrating traffic to healthy model pools, increasing capacity, and monitoring for regression.
Estimated next update: <60 minutes>

IC: <Incident commander name>
Primary on-call: <Primary name>
Ticket: <internal incident link>

We will provide a detailed post-incident summary after services are fully restored.

---
Template for postmortem notification to customers (short):
Subject: Incident summary: <Incident short id> — impact and remediation
Hello <Customer Name>,

Summary: On <date/time> we experienced <brief impact>. Services were restored by <time>. Root cause: <short root cause>.
What we did: <high level actions and current mitigations>.
Actions planned: <list of engineering and operational follow-ups>.

If you’d like a deeper technical briefing, we can schedule a call.

Section D — Example runbook snippets (copyable)
Runbook: High P95 latency for Hosted Text API - Symptoms: P95 increased >1500ms for 10m; increased request queue length; worker busy ratio >80%.
- Immediate checks:
  1) Check deployment health dashboard: /dashboards/hosted-text-api-health
  2) Confirm node-level memory and GPU utilization for model pools (query: gpu_util_by_pool > 75%).
  3) Inspect recent autoscale events and error logs for OOM or kernel failures.
- Mitigations (ordered):
  1) Trigger traffic migration to warm pool: CLI snippet:
     rbin infra migrate-traffic --service hosted-text-api --from pool-A --to pool-B --dry-run=false
  2) Increase target replicas for pool-B:
     rbin infra scale --pool pool-B --replicas +3 --priority urgent
  3) If memory OOMs are observed, reduce batch size via runtime flag for affected replicas until stable.

Runbook: Model-serving OOM cascade - Symptoms: repeated OOM logs, instance restarts, increased 5xx errors.
- Immediate checks: container OOM logs, kernel trace, model quantization profile in use.
- Fast mitigation: mark affected nodes unschedulable and shift traffic; revert last model change if one was recently deployed.

Section E — Game day and validation guidance
Objectives for game days - Validate rotation handoffs, escalation timeboxes, IC formation, and customer comms cadence.
- Exercise cross-team coordination (SRE, Runtime, Platform, Customer Success).

Run a quarterly scenario checklist
1) Simulated Sev-1: full region outage -> verify IC stands up within 10 minutes and Exec notified in <60 minutes.
2) Simulated gradual degradation: rolling latency increase -> verify escalation to IC within 25 minutes and status page updates at 30-min cadence.
3) Communications dry run: craft status-page and email drafts within 15 minutes of IC formation.

Success metrics (post-game-day)
- Ack time median < 3 minutes.
- Time-to-IC formation < 20 minutes.
- Status update drafts produced within 15 minutes of IC formation in 90% of exercises.
- Postmortem completed within 72 hours for simulated Sev-1.

Section F — Ownership, tooling links, and escalation contacts
Ownership - On-call schedule and rosters: /confluence/eng-sre/oncall-roster
- IC roster and escalation matrix: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/ic-roster-2025

Critical tooling
- Alerting dashboard: https://observability.redwood.internal/dashboards/alerts
- Status page editor: https://status.redwood.internal/editor
- Pager system: we use PagerDuty for primary/secondary pages (config docs in /confluence/eng-platform/pagerduty-config).

Escalation contacts (examples, use PagerDuty contact cadences in practice)
- Primary: automatic page to Primary on-call
- Secondary: escalation after 5 minutes
- IC: escalate by pressing "IC" button in PagerDuty or pinging #incidents slack channel with /ic-start
- Executive contact: only for Sev-1 after 60 minutes unresolved

Appendix: quick reference cheat-sheet (stick this in on-call Slack channel)
- First 5 minutes: acknowledge or delegate
- Minutes 5–25: triage, document scope, attempt mitigation
- Minute 25: escalate to IC if unresolved
- Minute 60: notify Exec and Customer Success for proactive outreach

Related documents and templates

- PagerDuty configuration guide: /confluence/eng-platform/pagerduty-config
